M03.result: Capability model assessed against all 6 required states and 5 required fields. 2 of 6 states expressible; sdk_version and sdk_compatible missing. Static/effective split is correct and the 'never advertise unregistered' rule is SATISFIED. Vocabulary decided: adopt Corpus CapabilityStatus.

M04.result: Neutral-result envelope implemented; FAILED != EMPTY now holds and is guarded by 13 tests. Found and fixed `or []` flattening of a falsy failed outcome.

M05.result: Option A with the tier boundary corrected: SearchCoordinator (Tier-L) holds the neutral orchestration; SearchService is a thin wire adapter. Corpus RetrievalIndex already existed, so Option B's extraction was already done. Closed MCP-D02 and MCP-M00-07; 5 of 6 MCP-M00-12 failures closed by fixing code.

M06.result: Schema/validation audit: input validation complete, declared schema matches enforcement, unsafe schemes blocked, content sanitised, traversal rejected, private seam isolated to one function. 4 new findings; 2 items deferred to M12.

M07.result: FIRST run with the real SDK. Suite: pristine 153 passed / this tree 166 passed / 0 failed. Closed M06's two deferred items and M06-04. Found and fixed M07-01 and M07-02: M04's status was dropped by the closed output model and never reported on the success path, so MCP-D03 held at Tier-L but FAILED at the wire.

M08.result: All 8 bundles reduce to one invocation, `python -m scikitplot.mcp`, EXECUTED over real stdio: tools listed, call succeeded, unknown-arg rejected. No embedded credentials in 17 JSON files. M02-01/M02-02 remain open.

M09.result: Verified through the real protocol: raw exceptions not exposed (a credential-bearing DSN was masked), injection payload carries the UNTRUSTED notice, file:// neutralised, health endpoint minimal, k/query bounded at two layers, semaphore bounds concurrency. Annotations are enforced, not merely advertised.

M10.result: No sampling/elicitation/roots/subscribe and no write-capable tools. The server is a passive read-only capability provider; the conditional sampling requirements do not apply.

M11.result: All M04/M05/M07 changes are ADDITIVE. Nothing removed from __all__; SearchService did not move; tool input schema and output required-fields identical to the pristine tree. New wire fields are optional, so existing clients are unaffected. No migration adapter needed.

M12.result: Live Streamable HTTP closed: server bound on 127.0.0.1:8000, existing harness RUN (27 passed, 1 optional skip), cancellation clean with health 200 after, 25-way concurrency 0 exceptions, SIGTERM -> ordered shutdown and port released with no orphan.
M12.cause: Needs a meson-python/Cython toolchain and multiple interpreters. Asserting wheel metadata without a built wheel would be INFERRED presented as VERIFIED.

M13.result: Closed 12 findings including the campaign's only live rejection-list violation (MCP-D01). Suite 166 -> 172 passed, 0 failed. Closure criteria 8/13 -> 11/13.

M14.result: Added local Corpus+Annoy CLI backend selection, deterministic HashEmbedder integration, stable resource lookup, and a CI-oriented Hamlet MCP gallery. Full offline MCP suite: 164 passed, 2 skipped. Native Annoy + MCP SDK live HTTP unavailable in this harness.

open_findings.title: The [mcp] extra contradicts the policy stated in its own comment; the test that would catch it is commented out
open_findings.evidence: pyproject.toml [mcp]: an 11-line comment states the SDK line must carry NO python marker; the next line is 'mcp>=2.0.0,<3; python_version >= "3.10"'. Effect: on 3.8/3.9 the extra resolves to pydantic-only instead of failing -- exactly the failure the comment describes.
open_findings.disabled_gate: test_mcp_import_surface.py::test_mcp_extra_declares_server_dependencies has its marker assertions commented out, leaving sdk_lines computed-and-unused and 'import re as _re' unused.
open_findings.blocked_by: MCP_COMPATIBILITY_POLICY.md is the adjudicating document and is missing -> M01 is BLOCKED.
open_findings.m00r: UNCHANGED and live: pyproject.toml byte-identical to the M00 tree; marker still present; still unadjudicable without the missing policy.
open_findings.correction: M00/M00-R said the extra 'violates policy'. More precisely: the marker SATISFIES guide sec6 (which forbids declaring mcp BELOW the SDK floor) while producing exactly the partial-extra failure its own in-file comment identifies.
open_findings.adjudication: Verified: mcp 2.0.0 Requires-Python >=3.10 (PyPI). Marker evaluation: on py3.8/3.9 the mcp requirement is DROPPED and pydantic survives, so pip install 'scikit-plots[mcp]' SUCCEEDS with no server. Removing the marker satisfies BOTH the guide and the comment; keeping it satisfies only the weaker rule. No trade-off exists, so MCP_COMPATIBILITY_POLICY.md is needed only to ratify.
open_findings.recommendation: Remove the python_version marker; re-enable the commented-out assertion in test_mcp_import_surface.py; record an ADR.
open_findings.resolution: python_version marker removed from the SDK line; disabled assertion re-enabled.

open_findings.title: The documented actionable SDK error is unreachable on the path all 8 plugin bundles use
open_findings.evidence: python -m scikitplot.mcp with no [mcp] -> raw 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named pydantic' traceback, exit 1. __main__.py:51 imports the _server MODULE, so _server.py:22 (module-scope pydantic) raises before the guarded SDK import at _server.py:274-283 can produce its message.
open_findings.unreachable_message: _server.py:280 'MCP SDK v2 is required for the server layer; on Python >= 3.10 install it with: pip install "mcp>=2.0.0,<3".' Only fires when pydantic is present but the SDK is not.
open_findings.compounding: __main__.py never calls server_runtime_status() before create_server() at line 564 (grep confirms zero references), though _capabilities.py:131 states that function exists precisely so callers avoid this exception.
open_findings.impact: Every plugin bundle declares 'python -m scikitplot.mcp'. A base-install user of Claude/Cursor/VSCode/Codex/Cline/Continue/Windsurf/OpenClaw gets a traceback naming pydantic, with no mention of the [mcp] extra.
open_findings.fix: M07: consult server_runtime_status() and exit with its reason before touching _server. Depends on MCP-D01 being fixed first, or the pre-flight reports server_available=True in the shadowing case.
open_findings.resolution: __main__.py pre-flights server_runtime_status() before touching the server tier; base install now gets an actionable SystemExit instead of a raw pydantic traceback.

open_findings.title: All 8 plugin bundles hard-code bare 'python' as the launch command
open_findings.evidence: Every bundle declares {'command': 'python', 'args': ['-m','scikitplot.mcp']}.
open_findings.risk: Many distributions ship only python3; where the client does not activate the venv, 'python' resolves to a system interpreter without scikit-plots, yielding 'No module named scikitplot' -- a different unhelpful failure.
open_findings.fix: sys.executable is unavailable in static JSON; document the prerequisite in plugins/README.md or give per-bundle absolute-interpreter guidance.

open_findings.title: Capability reporting cannot express 4 of the 6 states the guide requires
open_findings.evidence: server_runtime_status()'s entire vocabulary is sdk_present:bool plus reason in {None,'python<3.10','mcp-sdk-not-installed'}. PRESENT_INCOMPATIBLE, BROKEN, MISCONFIGURED and UNKNOWN have no representation.
open_findings.aggravating: A client receiving server_available:true cannot tell whether that was probed or assumed.
open_findings.fix: Adopt Corpus CapabilityStatus and add sdk_version/sdk_compatible. M03-01, M03-02 and MCP-D01 resolve together or not at all.
open_findings.resolution: All six required states expressible via the Corpus-mirrored CapabilityStatus vocabulary.

open_findings.title: A present-but-broken SDK install reports as PRESENT_COMPATIBLE
open_findings.evidence: Constructed mcp/__init__.py raising ImportError (shape of a corrupt or ABI-mismatched package): server_runtime_status() -> server_available True, sdk_present True, reason None, while 'import mcp' raises.
open_findings.distinct_from_D01: D01 is a false positive from PATH SHADOWING; this is a false positive from an UNHEALTHY INSTALL. Same root: find_spec answers locatability, not importability or version.
open_findings.resolution: Probing uses importlib.metadata.version + range check, so a broken/incompatible SDK is no longer reported as compatible.

open_findings.title: Probe failure is silently reported as ABSENT rather than UNKNOWN
open_findings.evidence: _capabilities.py:168-171 `except (ImportError, ValueError): return False`. A failed probe means UNKNOWN; reporting False means 'not installed, go install it', which may be wrong.
open_findings.violates: MAINTENANCE_MODEL.md: 'An unverified claim is worse than a narrow one. Prefer UNKNOWN or a declared degradation over a confident guess.'
open_findings.cross_module: Corpus ALREADY FIXED THIS EXACT DEFECT and recorded why. corpus/_capabilities.py CapabilityStatus docstring: 'Finding F-R02-05 measured that a backend whose is_available() RAISED -- an installed but corrupt, mis-linked or ABI-incompatible native library -- reported exactly the same as one that was never installed.' MCP's _present() reproduces the defect Corpus retired. Cite F-R02-05 in the ADR.
open_findings.resolution: A failed probe returns UNKNOWN, never ABSENT.

open_findings.title: create_server registers the health route with no transport awareness
open_findings.evidence: create_server gates only on `if health_path is not None:` (_server.py:335) and takes NO transport parameter. effective_server_capabilities reports health only for streamable-http. Diverges in 2 of 8 configurations: stdio + health_path set.
open_findings.why_cli_is_safe: __main__.py:568 passes health_path=None unless transport=='streamable-http'. The invariant therefore holds by CALLER CONVENTION, not by construction -- the MCP-M00-05 / MCP-M00-07 pattern again.
open_findings.compounds_M01_01: The documented default create_server(retriever) has health_path='/healthz', so it executes `from starlette.requests import ...` (_server.py:341) -- requiring an UNDECLARED dependency to register a route the default stdio transport cannot serve.
open_findings.evidence_class: VERIFIED by control-flow reading; not executed (create_server needs pydantic + SDK). Runtime confirmation belongs to M12.
open_findings.fix: Make create_server transport-aware, or default health_path=None so the route is opt-in. Sequence with M07.
open_findings.resolution: create_server(health_path=...) now defaults to None; the HTTP route is opt-in.

open_findings.title: An uncoercible score is coerced to a legitimate 0.0
open_findings.evidence: nan, inf, -inf, 'abc' and None all emerge as 0.0. 0.0 is a valid similarity score, so 'unusable' is indistinguishable from 'genuinely zero'.
open_findings.pattern: Same shape as M03-03 (_present() -> False for a failed probe) and MCP-D05 (BROKEN reported as ABSENT). Three sites, one habit.
open_findings.fix: Emit None for an uncoercible score.
open_findings.deferral_reason: The honest fix changes the advertised output schema (CitationOutput.score is a typed float; making it nullable would break a strict client). M11 established every change so far is additive; not traded for a P3 late in the campaign. Belongs with a schema version bump.

open_findings.title: '.' and '..' are accepted as document identifiers
open_findings.evidence: _DOC_ID_RE = \A[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,200}\Z accepts '.' and '..'; ':' is accepted too. Full traversal is blocked ('/' excluded), verified across 12 identifiers.
open_findings.why_it_matters: document_reader is caller-supplied third-party code; a reader doing Path(base)/doc_id receives a directory reference. On Windows ':' permits drive-relative or ADS forms.
open_findings.fix: Exclude '.', '..' and a leading ':'. Narrows no legitimate identifier.

open_findings.title: Non-URI strings are emitted as citation URIs
open_findings.evidence: 'not a uri' -> 'not a uri#a'. Dangerous schemes ARE blocked (javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript: -> ''), so this is not a security hole, but a citation whose URI is not a URI is a broken citation a client may render as a link.
open_findings.fix: Reject it (empty, as with blocked schemes) or validate it parses as a relative reference.
open_findings.deferral_reason: Dangerous schemes are already blocked, so this is cosmetic correctness; tightening risks rejecting legitimate relative references.

open_findings.title: The same retrieval failure maps to two different wire outcomes
open_findings.evidence: One retriever with a down backend, varying only `strict`: strict=False -> RESULT isError=True retrieval_status='failed'; strict=True -> RAISES RuntimeError('documentation search is temporarily unavailable').
open_findings.analysis: `strict` was a diagnostic control. After M04 it also selects the wire error channel. Not a regression: the divergence pre-existed but was invisible because the non-strict path lied (EMPTY / isError False). M04 made both truthful and thereby exposed that they are two paths.
open_findings.recommendation: Make structuredContent.retrieval_status + isError canonical -- it carries per-leg detail, whereas RuntimeError collapses everything to one opaque sentence. Keep `strict` for logging only. Decide in M07.
open_findings.blocks: Mapping Corpus ErrorRecord.code/ErrorCategory onto the wire (deferred from M04) -- the destination depends on which channel wins.
open_findings.resolution: search_docs now raises on a FAILED outcome, so both strict modes yield is_error=True at the protocol level. `strict` is a diagnostic control again.

open_findings.title: M04's retrieval status never reached the MCP wire
open_findings.evidence: Protocol measurement: strict=False -> is_error=False, retrieval_status=None. SearchDocsOutput is a closed model (extra=forbid) whose field list lacked retrieval_status/retrieval_errors, so pydantic SILENTLY DROPPED them; SearchService also read only structuredContent and never raw['isError'].
open_findings.significance: MCP-D03 held at Tier-L and FAILED at the wire -- the only externally observable place. This was a gap in M04's own verification and is exactly the failure the guide's rule 'do not infer transport correctness from unit-level direct function calls' names.
open_findings.fix: retrieval_status and retrieval_errors added as documented optional fields; SearchService propagates both.

open_findings.title: The success path never reported retrieval status
open_findings.evidence: build_search_docs_result set retrieval_status only in its `if not safe:` branch, so any result WITH hits carried no status.
open_findings.significance: DEGRADED was invisible exactly when it matters most -- a partial result that still returns passages. A client inspecting only `count` would never learn evidence was missing.
open_findings.fix: Success path now reports status and surfaces retrieval_errors. Verified: fusion fail+ok -> is_error=False, status='degraded', count=1, errors=['index down'].

open_findings.title: The SDK-missing guard misreports any transitive ImportError as 'SDK not installed'
open_findings.evidence: With starlette blocked but mcp installed, create_server raises 'MCP SDK v2 is required ... pip install mcp>=2.0.0,<3'. The SDK IS installed; the guard caught an ImportError from inside the SDK's own dependency chain.
open_findings.pattern: Fourth site of one habit, after M03-03, MCP-D05 and M06-01: converting 'something is wrong in a way I did not check' into a confident, specific, wrong claim.
open_findings.resolution: create_server consults the capability probe and distinguishes absent / incompatible / broken-environment.

corpus_contracts_to_map.RetrievalResponse/RetrievalStatus: M04 core question: DEGRADED is neither success nor error on the wire
corpus_contracts_to_map.ErrorRecord: already JSON-serialisable; reuse rather than inventing a second error shape

lessons.title: A missing document is not automatically a blocker
lessons.context: M00-R marked M01 BLOCKED pending MCP_COMPATIBILITY_POLICY.md.
lessons.issue: M01 was substantially answerable: the guide states the packaging rule itself (sec6), and marker semantics plus the SDK's published Requires-Python settle MCP-M00-10 deterministically.
lessons.root_cause: Treated 'the adjudicating document is missing' as 'the question is unanswerable' without walking the evidence precedence list. The guide sits at rank 1-3 (snapshot / deterministic reproducers / package metadata); the missing policy is rank 5 (source-side maintenance documents).
lessons.prevention_rule_when: a run is about to be marked BLOCKED on a missing document
lessons.prevention_rule_then: walk the evidence precedence list top-down and record, per blocked item, which rank could settle it; mark BLOCKED only for items no higher-ranked source can reach, and PARTIAL for the rest
lessons.verified_by: any BLOCKED item in STATE.json names the precedence ranks checked and why each failed
